name: Aerospace
boundaries: Aerospace: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The useful sustained-flight capability is retained without requiring one engine to cover every flight regime or assuming affordable orbital access.

Low-boom overland flight could be valuable, but faster service alone was judged below the requested impact threshold. Complete elimination of ground-level sound and automatic removal of restrictions are unsupported.
SSTO is one possible route to mass access, but a stage count is not necessary to the revolutionary outcome. The claimed cost below $100/kg and airline-like frequency are not established.

Durable large-area laminar flow could save fuel, but the asserted whole-aircraft drag and fuel reductions are not established, and the concept was judged an efficiency advance rather than a separate revolution at this threshold. Flight research already addresses practical barriers: Mia Siochi and colleagues, “Mitigation of Insect Residue Contamination on Hybrid Laminar Flow Control Leading Edge Surfaces: Part 1,” NASA technical report record, abstract, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20200004824, says insect residue can cause “loss of laminar flow.” The record’s abstract was inspected; the full paper was not assessed.

Such materials could be important, but the claimed 20–30% engine-efficiency jump does not follow from the temperature specification alone. An unverified material target and prospective component gain do not establish a qualifying aircraft-level transformation.

original_dispositions.original_title: Universal plasma or electromagnetic flow control
original_dispositions.reason: Flow control could enable useful designs, but eliminating separation at every speed and angle, replacing all control surfaces and delivering stall-free flight are not established. No particular demonstrated or sufficiently bounded aerospace capability was identified here that meets the threshold.

Adaptable structures could improve aircraft, but the “no penalty” condition and 15–25% gains across all missions are unsupported. The stated concept is principally an unquantified optimization without a demonstrated transformative system-level outcome.
The revised concept centers on the large, long-range aircraft capability and does not assume that a battery-specific-energy figure is sufficient.

Resilient navigation is important, but centimeter accuracy for months without any external reference is an exceptionally strong unverified specification; a sensor breakthrough alone does not establish it. A NASA-hosted assessment notes both atom-interferometer strengths and practical complexity: NASA, “Quantum Sensors for Space Science,” presentation, atom-interferometer findings, slide 26, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20250004940/downloads/Singh-QS-Presentation%20at%20NAS.pdf?attachment=true, describes “moderately complex instruments.” The full assessment and a quantitative mission-level case were not evaluated here.

Low-maintenance reusable thermal protection could help achieve mass-access orbital transport. Self-healing and adaptive emissivity are possible approaches, but their separate necessity and transformative effect are not established.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Retained AER-01 through AER-08 and their distinct identities. Clarified that AER-07’s 140-meter survey target does not establish civilization-scale defense, and flagged the possible AER-05/AER-06 relationship.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The survey target and objective do not by themselves establish defense against civilization-threatening impacts. Orbital power stations might use the construction capability; either concept could be demonstrated without establishing the other.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Added AER-09 for the historical hypersonic concept.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Judged by an integrated, sustained flight capability rather than a universal engine or a promise of cheap orbital access.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Added AER-10 for the historical electric-aircraft concept. Incorporated the July 2026 hybrid flight demonstration.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Judged by a complete large, fossil-fuel-free long-range aircraft rather than a specified battery number.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Did not add quiet supersonic flight.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The first pass assessed it below this list’s impact threshold, although it remains a consequential research goal. NASA’s October 28, 2026 update says the X-59 had reached Mach 1.53 and was transitioning toward acoustic validation; it did not establish quiet commercial service. Source: Kristen Hatfield, NASA, “NASA Celebrates a Year of Progress Since First X-59 Flight,” October 28, 2026, opening paragraphs, https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/quesst/2026/10/28/nasa-celebrates-a-year-of-progress-since-first-x-59-flight/: “transition toward a new phase of testing: acoustic validation.” No DOI identified.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Removed the historical list’s unsupported exact benefit figures and universal claims from the revised concepts and disposition.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The impact judgments remain conditional rather than forecasts.
